{{recipesummary | category = Sauce recipes | time = Prep: 10 minutes
Cooking: time varies | difficulty = 2 | energy = ~100 Cal }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Sauces|Sauces]] '''Senf''' is German for "mustard". This particular senf, known as 'Süßer Senf', has a sweet, yet sharp taste that makes it great on sandwiches and crackers. While this recipe is from a 3rd or 4th generation German American, such recipes are said to originate from the southern parts of Germany (Bavaria). ==Ingredients== *1.7 [[Cookbook:Oz|oz]] dry ground [[Cookbook:Mustard|mustard]] *½ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]] *½ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]] *½ tsp [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]] *[[Cookbook:Pepper|pepper]] ==Procedure== # Mix sugar, mustard, salt, and pepper together. Mix in water. # Mix in vinegar last, as the mustard will lose some of its flavour if vinegar is introduced too early. # Stir using a wire [[Cookbook:Whisk|whisk]] to prevent lumps. # Add some water if too thick. ==Notes, tips, and variations== * It gets better as it cools and ages awhile. [[Category:German recipes|{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Recipes for sauces and condiments|{{PAGENAME}}]] [[Category:Recipes using sugar]] [[Category:Recipes using mustard powder]]
